featured_reviews.name: Neelachandra Tawde
featured_reviews.review_text: Sassoon Dock, with its rich history, cultural significance, and bustling fishing activity, offers a glimpse into Mumbai's maritime heritage. As a vibrant and dynamic space, it continues to be an integral part of the city's life, serving as a testament to the coexistence of tradition and modernity. Whether for its historical value, its thriving fishing community, or its cultural vitality, Sassoon Dock stands as an enduring symbol of Mumbai's coastal legacy and its deep-rooted connection with the Arabian Sea.

featured_reviews.name: rajesh jaiswar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Sassoon Dock Jetty, located in Colaba, is one of Mumbai’s oldest and most active jetties, offering a real glimpse into the city’s fishing and maritime life. Early mornings are the best time to visit, as you can see fishermen unloading their fresh catch, boats docking, and the local fish market coming alive with energy. The atmosphere is bustling and full of authentic coastal charm.

The jetty area has improved over time, with better cleanliness and organization. The view of the Arabian Sea and the colorful fishing boats make it a great spot for photography and exploring Mumbai’s heritage side. It’s also known for its connection to the Sassoon Dock Art Project, where murals and street art add a creative touch to the surroundings.

Visitors should be prepared for some fishy smells and wet floors, but the experience is truly worth it for those wanting to see Mumbai’s working waterfront up close.

Overall, Sassoon Dock Jetty is a lively, historic, and culturally rich spot that reflects the true coastal spirit of Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Shaibaz Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Sassoon Dock is a historic and bustling fish market located in Mumbai, India. Named after the prominent Sassoon family, who were influential in the development of Mumbai during the British colonial era, this dock has been a vital hub for the city's fishing industry for over a century.

Key features and highlights of Sassoon Dock include:

1. Fishing Hub: Sassoon Dock is one of Mumbai's oldest fishing docks and continues to play a crucial role in the seafood industry. It serves as a primary landing point for fishermen who bring in their catch from the Arabian Sea.

2. Vibrant Fish Market: The area around Sassoon Dock is teeming with activity, especially in the early morning when the day's catch is unloaded and sold. The market is a vibrant and colorful scene with a wide variety of seafood on display, including fish, crabs, prawns, and more.

3. Local Culture: Visiting Sassoon Dock provides a unique glimpse into the local fishing culture of Mumbai. It's an opportunity to witness the daily routines and traditions of the fishermen and fisherwomen who depend on this livelihood.

4. Photography Destination: The visual spectacle of Sassoon Dock, with its bustling market and picturesque boats, has made it a popular spot for photographers and tourists. The vibrant chaos and the play of light and shadow create captivating scenes for photography enthusiasts.

5. Heritage Value: Sassoon Dock is a heritage site that reflects Mumbai's history as a bustling port city. The architecture of the dock and its surroundings showcase a blend of British colonial and local architectural styles.

6. Conservation Efforts: In recent years, there have been efforts to modernize and improve the facilities at Sassoon Dock while also addressing environmental concerns. Initiatives to promote sustainable fishing practices and reduce the dock's ecological footprint have gained attention.

Sassoon Dock is not just a place of economic significance but also a cultural and historical landmark in Mumbai. It offers a sensory-rich experience for visitors, whether they are interested in the seafood trade, photography, or simply wish to immerse themselves in the vibrant local atmosphere.

featured_reviews.name: Rajib Saarkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Fish Market at Four Bunglow is one of the most authentic and vibrant seafood destinations in the city. If you’re a seafood lover, this place is a treasure trove. The market comes alive early in the morning with a wide variety of freshly caught fish, prawns, crabs, and even rare seasonal catches that you won’t easily find in supermarkets. The stalls are well-organized, and many vendors are friendly, knowledgeable, and willing to clean or cut the fish as per your requirement, which makes the whole experience convenient.

What stands out most is the freshness—there is a noticeable difference in taste compared to store-bought seafood. Prices are also quite reasonable, and with some bargaining, you can get excellent deals, especially if you’re buying in bulk. Regular customers often know which vendors offer the best catch of the day, so it’s worth exploring a bit before making your pick.

The market does get crowded during peak hours, especially weekends, but that adds to the bustling, energetic vibe. A pro tip is to go early in the morning to get the best selection. Since it’s a traditional fish market, be prepared for the typical sights, sounds, and smells, but that’s part of its charm and authenticity.

Overall, the Fish Market at Four Bunglow is not just a place to buy seafood—it’s an experience in itself. Freshness, variety, and local flavor all come together here, making it a must-visit for seafood enthusiasts.

featured_reviews.review_text: The Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute was established in the government of India on 3 February 1947 under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare and later, in 1967, it joined the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) family and emerged as a leading tropical marine fisheries research institute in the world. The Headquarters of the ICAR-CMFRI is located in Kochi, Kerala. Initially the institute focused its research efforts on creating a strong database on marine fisheries sector by developing scientific methodologies for estimating the marine fish landings and effort inputs, taxonomy of marine organisms and the biological aspects of the exploited stocks of finfish and shellfish on which fisheries management were to be based. This focus contributed significantly to development of the marine fisheries sector from a predominantly artisanal, sustenance fishery till the early sixties to that of a complex, multi-gear, multi-species fisheries. featured_reviews.name: Ashish Chavan
featured_reviews.review_text: A fantastic place to unwind from your busy corporate life. Whether you love angling (fishing) or not... take a flat bottom boat n let it gently drift in the lake while you soak in the nature n read a book. Possibly the only club thats open 24 x 7; 365 days. Monsoons are magical here...

featured_reviews.name: Savvy Bajaj
featured_reviews.review_text:
Any place of worship is beautiful. . Just wanted to share I am a hindu, and I love coming to this local church in our residential  area which displays a sense of oneness towards all members.  This picture is of the Annual summer camp  it hosts with the youth of the church coming together to welcome and  embrace children from all walks of lives under its roof.

The fact that these  youths of today are spending quality time with the kids emulating  the finest details of good living like sharing, team work, empathy, leading and even humility is a great initiative. We are blessed to have goodness in our lives.

featured_reviews.name: Fatema Motorwala
featured_reviews.review_text: The paintings the antique and the ambience everything is so cool. Alot of amazing and unique collection with a variety of range.

featured_reviews.name: Himadri Palai
featured_reviews.review_text:
I've visited so many art galleries. But this one was so different. The ambience this one provides is so different from other art galleries in Mumbai.

It is located in Byculla. It's not very far from Byculla station. You can even go walking or just take a taxi outside railway station.

Exhibition inside was beautiful. They also have a pond inside which has swans and frogs. It looks very pretty during the day. Interiors of this gallery is too good.

Everyone should visit this gallery atleast once. Loved it!

featured_reviews.name: Kajal Gaitonde
featured_reviews.review_text:
It is a wonderful space, actively engaging in creating Art Awareness for public. One should try to participate in their Art-centric activities on a regular basis.
The pictures that I have posted is another gallery in the same vicinity, a little ahead from there. If you visit Nine Fish AG, do not miss visiting this beautiful, glass structure Art Gallery too.

featured_reviews.name: Harsh Pandya
featured_reviews.review_text: Was here for an exhibition. It has a huge hall for the main set of artworks and a smaller room at the back for more. Can easily accomodate larger artworks/ sculpture as seen in photo. Acoustics are great to host a talk/ presentation. Lighting and display are done with finesse and it has a class of its own . It's located in a peaceful compound with a few more galleries to explore.

featured_reviews.name: Bansri Chavda
featured_reviews.review_text: Ninefish is retreat for lost old souls , with art and the premises that speak of books, art. Poetry , antiques, thick vegetation, old pond room, ceramic studio , print studio ..... and it has more dimensions! Explore for yourself

featured_reviews.name: Rekha Krishnan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Beautiful space for exhibiting. The architecture of the gallery is interesting. The old mill structure has been retained, with careful alterations. The walls with their rough texture create an 'old world' environment.
The different rooms are used to display a variety of work.
The location is a bit difficult to find, since it is inside the Great Eastern Mills compound.

featured_reviews.name: Saurabh Chavan
featured_reviews.review_text: This is one of the hidden art galleries in Mumbai. Aesthetic ambience with vintage things. Great.

featured_reviews.name: Pottery by Mangala
featured_reviews.review_text: An excellent gallery space to showcase your creative work be it art , photographs or ceramics . . I have been to some wonderfully curated exhibitions in this gallery .
